run.prompt: Draw an animated SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle. Make the wheels turn and the pelican pedal. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
run.notes: Scaffolded by the same engineering pipeline that produced the other animated submissions: a Python script in /tmp computed 24 phase samples per 1.6 s pedal revolution and baked them into CSS @keyframes for both legs, the body bob, the wing flap, the scarf flutter and the fish-tail wiggle. Two-bone IK (thigh 82, shin 92, crank radius 36, forward knee) is solved so both feet track the pedal spindles exactly; nested pedal groups counter-rotate at the crank rate to keep the pedals level. Wheels, chainring and crank arms spin via simple CSS rotation; clouds drift and road dashes plus chain runs animate via translateX and stroke-dashoffset; a prefers-reduced-motion media query disables every animation class. Color palette differs from step-5-preview (lavender body, pink pouch, blue scarf, cool grey-blue legs) so this card is visually distinguishable. Headless Chrome render-check verified the reduced-motion poster is byte-identical to the rendered first frame and that the 1.6 s frame matches the 0 s frame. Model identity MiniMax-M3 is the name the system reports and is not independently verified, so model.id is null; provider MiniMax is the model's origin, also not independently verified. Known cosmetic defects recorded rather than corrected: chain runs are animated dashed strokes rather than linked chains; both legs share one screen plane; hips are fixed so the body bob is cosmetic and not driven by leg IK; the saddle is mostly occluded by the body; the fish is static except its tail; clouds loop discontinuously at the wrap point; no audio; transitions are linear only.
